releases.displayName: Winter Progress Update! Big News Soon!

items.text: Hello Survivors!
Since the holidays ended, we've been hunkering down and working on all things Outbreak: Shades of Horror! We wanted to come up for air and give you all a quick update on what we've been up to!

First, thank you to everyone who has played the Steam & Xbox Series X|S versions of the game, spread the word, and given us feedback! We are thrilled that everyone is playing and enjoying the ongoing Winter Wonderland and DINOBREAK crossover content! We will continue to update and improve the game based on player feedback.
Speaking of seasonal content, we're hard at work on the next seasonal event, which is coming this Spring! Once we're a little closer to deployment, we'll have more information to share.
We're still finalizing timelines and specifics, but there's a lot of other stuff coming up! Here's a small preview on top of the aforementioned seasonal content...
You can expect news regarding cross-platform multiplayer in the next few weeks.
New DLC content is being planned for release down the line.
Work continues on the PlayStation 5 version of the game. We'll share more details as we approach Spring!
Progress on Story Mode remains steady. This is another area we'll be talking more about in the Spring!

We want to take this time to thank everyone for their support and patience as we've continued to build out Outbreak: Shades of Horror. Game development is no easy task, and with a game as cutting edge as Shades of Horror that includes a large amount of content, features, and supported platforms, it's certainly challenging as a small indie team to craft.
We're extremely excited for you all to enjoy what we've been working so hard on, so we humbly ask for a little more time before we share and release our next wave of zombie-slaying mayhem.
Until next time, take care Survivors!
Hello Survivors!

notes.title: First, check out this new trailer

items.text: Today, we're going to break down the game's modes and hub area for you! The entirety of Outbreak: Shades of Horror can be experienced either solo or with up to three friends in co-op play over the network.
Cypress Reel

This playground is where you and your friends can group up and enter the game's various modes! You can select your character (across over 25 options!) and practice your controls, and you can also test your mettle at the obstacle course, improve your combat prowess, check out the game's various abilities and items, and so much more! Over time, Cypress Reel will expand with new content and special events!
Story mode

This is the survival horror campaign you're all expecting! Manage your resources and inventory, defeat menacing zombies, solve puzzles, and find notes as you explore colossal maps with awesome set-pieces and challenging encounters. Each episode will play out in explosive fashion, with multiple routes and many secrets to discover.
Invasion mode

A different flavor of survival. You'll face down endless enemy hordes as you attempt to both live and protect innocents. Before the game begins, you have a small period of time to fortify your base with turrets, traps, and more. Once the creatures appear, you'll need to annihilate hundreds of them without losing all of your lives or your civilians in the heat of battle. Multiple maps will be available!
Raid mode

This arcade-style experience is a blast. Scout sprawling, tight maps, take on the undead masses, and rescue trapped civilians before time runs out! As with the rest of Outbreak: Shades of Horror, Raid mode will be updated with new content and maps over time. Fans of our previous games may even find some fun nods to our history.
Mini-games

For some quick action, check out a selection of extra game types inspired by classic survival horror masterpieces. From Boss Rush, where you'll face a parade of tough monsters, to Collapse, where you'll flee a nasty subway on the brink of destruction, these scenarios are fun to play through over and over. Look forward to new mini-games as the game continues to grow!

We hope you're excited to experience the wild world of Cypress Ridge when Outbreak: Shades of Horror begins its descent onto Xbox Series, PlayStation 5, and on PC via Steam this year! We will of course continue to update you with the latest information and more specific release timing as development continues. Thank you as always for your support and patience.

releases.displayName: Railbreak VR & Tailbreak Campaign + Railbreak Content Update One Arrives Aug 30t

items.text: Hey Survivors!
Wow, we have a lot to talk about and a busy week ahead! Let's get to it!

notes.title: Railbreak VR & Tailbreak Crowdfunding Campaign is LIVE on Jan 30th @ 1PM ET!

items.text: Everyone has been asking for it, so we're doing it! Back our BackerKit Crowdfunding Campaign on Jan 30th @ 1PM ET to help make Railbreak VR on SteamVR and Tailbreak for both Railbreak and Railbreak VR happen!

Railbreak VR is exactly what it sounds like - a full native standalone implementation of SteamVR for all of Railbreak (and Tailbreak!). Experience the sights and sounds through your cutting edge VR headset as you take on the waves of glitched infected and dinos in the over-the-top insanity of the world of Railbreak!

Tailbreak is our first full sized story expansion pack for Railbreak. Bringing our dinos from Dinobreak into the world of Railbreak, you'll be fighting through a brand new story, new game modes, using new characters and weapons, and tons more! It's dinoriffic and we can't wait for it!

And we're going to have some absolutely INSANE giveaways! So go follow our Backerkit Crowdfunding page right now at http://www.railbreakvr.com so you don't miss your chance to back the project, and get in on these amazing giveaways!
We'll also be streaming all day starting at 1PM ET on twitch.tv/deaddropstudios !

notes.title: Railbreak Content Update One - Time Korrisis - Arrives on Jan 30th, 2024!

items.text: Our first content update is coming to Railbreak on all platforms on Jan 30th! Featuring the brand new Time Korrisis mode that is playable in every part of Railbreak, you'll be racing the clock as you fight through the undead to score more time and survive the nightmare! You can play this mode across all of Railbreak, so think of it as a new game plus!

We also have our new character, Korrine the Glitch Goddess, joining the cast! She's our first expert level character and she's challenging but incredibly fun to use. She uses all new projectile weapons (instead of the hitscan of other characters) and boasts the beastly Plasma Cannon, Glitched Sidearm, and the Katana which has the ability to trigger super glitches! Get ready for a brand new experience!
We'll be back on Tuesday with more news, but get ready for some crazy antics and follow the BackerKit Crowdfunding campaign now at http://www.railbreakvr.com so you're ready! (AND TELL YOUR FRIENDS!)
See you on Tuesday!
Hey Survivors,

Our latest patch for Railbreak is now live on Steam! This patch brings some meaty graphical enhancements to the game, and brings the title up to the 12GB size that was advertised on the store page since launch. If you encounter any instability, just reduce the Texture Quality setting in the Video Settings menu as that area received the biggest upgrade across the game.

Significant graphics improvements across the entire game. Hard drive space usage increased, however run-time RAM usage only appears slightly higher in-game as per our testing. This change does not affect the game's framerate.
Fixed an issue where the Sinden Lightgun Border would disappear on the Game Over screen.
Hey Survivors!
Good news! A few more glitches have been patched in the world of Railbreak on Steam! These patches are rolling out to all other platforms today as well!
Here's what we did, and don't forget to check the "Update Notes" button on the title screen for this complete list too! We have plenty more updates coming in the weeks ahead!
Added a "Compile Shaders" button to the Settings menu.
Added the Update Notes screen.
High scores now properly save in all parts of the game.
Added an option in Audio Settings to allow you to set the character's voice volume level independently.
Fixed numerous infrequent softlocks on Acts 2, 4, 5, and 6.
Added an option in Game Settings to allow you to specify additional wait time before moving to another area to make it easier to collect items.
Added an option to the Screen Filter Override in the Game Settings menu called "Never Switch", which will ensure no game overlays ever appear on screen.
Added an option to the Game Settings to specify larger bounding boxes on item pickups. This can only be set at the Main Menu.
Items can now only be picked up if they're visible to the player, and cannot be collected through walls or other surfaces anymore.
Improvements to eliminate a very infrequent situation where being grabbed by a zombie would remove your gun.
Additional performance improvements across the title.
Item highlights now appear at greater range.

releases.displayName: Outbreak: Epidemic Major Content Update Coming Feb 12th, 2020!

items.text: Hey Survivors!

We're happy to announce that Outbreak: Epidemic will leave Steam Early Access on Feb 12th, 2020 with the release of a brand new major content update! It will also release on Xbox One at the same time.

notes.title: What can we expect in the update?

items.text: You'll be fighting across six brand new scenarios in two new locations, the Tunnels and the Streets. After their harrowing escape from the underground morgue and repairing the train, the survivors find themselves trapped in the city's subway system. You'll need to blast your way up to the street-level if you want to escape. Then on the streets, the survivors will be confronted by both defusing a nuclear bomb and repairing their means of escape.

This update will bring Outbreak: Epidemic up to 18 total scenarios across the Campaign, Onslaught and Experiments modes. In addition, numerous gameplay fixes, tweaks and minor enhancements are included based on the months of testing the game has gone through. It's going to be a massive expansion to the series.

Outbreak: Epidemic will have reached a point with this update that it is fully functional and playable from start to finish. The majority of major bugs have been eliminated and the game plays great in both single-player and up to 4-player co-op. In addition, you have 18 scenarios to fight across (fully in co-op if you choose!). It makes sense to bring the game to a larger audience now.

notes.title: But is this the end of development for the game?

items.text: Of course not! Like all other titles in the Outbreak series, this title will continue to get new content. I'll be looking for the players to suggest in the discussion boards what they'd like to see more of: features, weapons, scenarios or fixes! Your feedback will directly drive where the game goes from here! So grab some friends, get some playtime in and send me your feedback on the forums!
Stay tuned for more information leading up to the release, including details on the Deluxe Edition DLC! Thank you for playing Epidemic and the entire Outbreak series. The best is yet to come!
Hey Survivors,

I've pushed a minor hotfix (v3.1) which fixes an issue where reading notes may softlock the game, or notes may appear in the wrong areas. Thanks to the players in the forums who reported this issue! ːsteamhappyː
Hey Survivors!
I'm excited to announce that v3.0 of Outbreak: Epidemic has been released, which features brand new scenarios, enhancements and fixes!

You now have access to the Depths campaign scenario, where the survivors will need to fight through a brutal underground maze to find safe passage into the city subway system. What horror will they uncover as they learn about the government's response to the epidemic? Grab your friends and experience the nightmare!

Next, check out the brand new Death Race experiments scenario! You have limited time to navigate the underground, find a necessary item and return to the train for repairs! Be careful - supply drops are spread thin and in dangerous areas - choose wisely when it's time to restock or when it's time to keep moving!
And finally, experience two brand new Onslaught Mode scenarios as you fight off waves of the undead in the underground!
All this new content takes place in a brand new location! In addition, this patch includes the following:
Ability to toggle your flashlight. (Bind this key in the Controls menu or restore your controls to default to use it if you've played before!)
Significant improvements to the spectator view to make it more smooth.
In-game UI and controls bug fixes to ensure menu navigation works correctly across keyboard and gamepad.
Significant improvements to enemy pathfinding to reduce cases of them getting stuck on game geometry.
Firing the shotgun when crouched no longer causes your player's animations to freeze.
Game size on disk, including memory used during gameplay, has been dramatically reduced.
Difficulty balancing and minor fixes across the entire game.
v3.0 also marks the transition of Outbreak: Epidemic to a paid title. Learn more about that decision here!
Note: If you purchased the Premium Content for Outbreak: Epidemic while it was a F2P title, you should still have access to the game. Reach out to me if you encounter any issues!
Thanks again for playing and I hope you enjoy the nightmare! Brand new content will be coming over the next several months!

releases.displayName: New Major Patch, Location & Major Game Changes Coming August 9th!

items.text: Hello Survivors!

We've had an awesome month since Outbreak: Epidemic launched on July 9th! We spent the first half of that month working on patches to address the largest feedback from the community quickly, and now we're happy to announce the next major patch is on the horizon and scheduled for August 9th!

But we have other news to share as well about the long term plans for the game including transitioning from a F2P title to a more classical paid title (and why that decision has been made, including how Premium Content owners will automatically keep their access to the game). So buckle up and keep reading for all the news!

After the survivors desperate attempt to call for help at the end of the Outbreak Scenario, they eventually learn that there's a military camp situated in a nearby urban center. With the undead roaming the countryside and a lack of a working vehicle, they take to the underground tunnels to try to find a way into the subway system underneath the city.
This leads them into the Depths, a dark and desolated underground system where they will learn horrifying truths about how the government tried to mitigate the epidemic.

On August 9th, you'll have access to a brand new Campaign scenario, two new Onslaught scenarios, and a new Experiments scenario. The campaign will take the survivors on a desperate quest to repair part of the underground subway system to make their way further into the city.

The new Experiments scenario increases the intensity by giving you 30 minutes to navigate the underground caverns to retrieve a desperately needed item before you make your escape. This guns blazing scenario will force you to move quickly, and carefully determine when you want to stop at a supply drop (scattered throughout the scenario) to re-arm. Be careful though, if you take too long, the caves will fill with gas and you'll be dead quickly.

This release on August 9th will come with Patch v3.0, which includes a large amount of small fixes and polish across the entire game (too much to list). It will also include heavily requested options like the ability to toggle your flashlight on or off during gameplay.

notes.title: Transitioning from Free To Play to a Traditional Paid Title on August 9th

items.text: I'm also ready to announce that Outbreak: Epidemic will be transitioning from a F2P title with optional premium content to a more traditional paid title like all of the other games in the Outbreak series. When I was planning to launch Epidemic, my goal was to open it to a larger community and invite everyone to play what was essentially a demo, with the option to upgrade to the full version.

After gathering feedback and observing the game's progress over the last month, it was determined that this model ultimately wouldn't allow the development of the game to proceed at the rate I want in the F2P model. It became clear that I would need to go in a route of creating and marketing add-on content like cosmetics to ensure the game remains financially viable, and that effort (with only a single developer working on the game) would greatly interfere with the development roadmap and timelines.

Transitioning to a paid title will allow me to focus on developing the core game experience including new scenarios, while not needing to focus on cosmetic or add-on content too early in the development process. It's definitely understandable if some folks will be unhappy with this decision, but I hope you'll understand that it's the best for the game long-term so it can stay on track and new content can be delivered at a reasonable clip.
To be clear - there are no plans to transition back to a F2P title for this game. It ultimately makes more sense as a more classical paid title.

notes.title: So how will the title work when the patch is released on August 9th?

items.text: For people who have purchased the Premium Content DLC, you will get access to the full paid game (as you've already paid for the upgrade). For anyone who has not upgraded to the Premium Content DLC and is only on the F2P version, unfortunately they will lose access to the title unless they purchase it. After speaking with Valve, this seemed like the best compromise for the title to ensure folks who have invested their money in the title get full access and their purchase remains valid.

Thank you to the entire community for supporting the Outbreak series and sharing such passionate feedback about the game. Epidemic has grown by leaps and bounds in the month since it launched and there's plenty of exciting new locations, content and more on the horizon. Thank you! :outbreakzombie:
We're happy to announce that v2.2 of Outbreak: Epidemic has been released!

New Onslaught Scenario - Two Stores. Fight the undead in the middle of a strip mall converted to a medical camp by the military shortly after the epidemic occurred. Featuring a large outdoor area with vertical options, as well as two indoor areas you can seamlessly enter and battle the undead in. This location does not take place in the Campaign and is simply a fun bonus map to mix things up!
Adjusted detection range based on enemy types and other qualifiers to improve some areas where enemies would become confused or stuck.
Minor cosmetic bug fixes across the scenarios.
We're happy to announce Outbreak: Epidemic v2.1 has been released!

This patch includes adjustments to increase the lethality of all non-reptile enemy types. Their movement speed is buffed and their detection range has been increased. To ensure this doesn't have any negative effects to spawn areas, you'll find the intros to the Tutorial, Outbreak and Darkness scenarios have been mildly changed.

Thanks again for playing and if you're enjoying the game, please be sure to consider leaving a positive review and sharing your thoughts! If you hit any issues, reach out anytime on our official Discord or on the forums and we can help out right away!
We're happy to announce Outbreak: Epidemic v2.0 has been released.
The player's laser sight will now smoothly update when moving.

The player camera now locks instantly to the player when rotating by default. This should greatly reduce the feeling of motion sickness. The old camera transition can still be enabled in the Options menu if you liked the slower transition effect.
Added a camera option to allow camera position transitions to be accelerated. You can enable this in the Options menu if you're interested.

The EXP & Leveling System has been overhauled to provide a more gentler leveling up curve at the lower levels. As you gain more levels, your progression will slow. You will see your new level reflected the next time you play the game.
Fixed an issue in the upstairs warehouse where enemies could become trapped on a chain link fence.
Leveling up is now reflected correctly mid-game, including having new buffs applied from the increased level.
Adjusted ammo amounts across the game.
We're happy to announce v1.9 of Outbreak: Epidemic has released!
When picking up stackable items, your inventory now more efficiently combines them with existing stacks before allocating to a new stack.
Slightly buffed ammo counts on Realism Mode across all scenarios.
Player facing the camera at all times is now enabled by default. This option can be changed in the Options menu. There will be no change if you've manually set this setting in the past.
Adjusted melee weapon damage in Realism Mode to ensure the Fire Axe and Sledgehammer are superior to the Knife for Renault.
Fixed numerous clipping issues on the multi-level warehouse.
Magnum damage now behaves properly on Realism Mode.
We're happy to announce Outbreak: Epidemic v1.8 has been released!

Adjusted handgun damage on Realism Mode to typically take at least 2-3 headshots to kill most low-level zombies with the Handgun. Characters with Handgun buffs will kill faster, those with debuffs will kill slower.
Weapons of the same type can now be combined to share ammo directly from the inventory.

When selecting a gun in your inventory, an Unload button will appear that will empty all remaining ammo if you have room. As a reminder, you can also combine a gun with an empty slot to unload its ammo.

Reduced Onslaught Mode wave intermission times in co-op. There is now less of a break between waves in co-op to keep the game moving at a good pace. Single-player still has the longer intermission times to give the player more of an opportunity to survive.
Fixed issues where guns would not detect hits on enemies due to other collisions intercepting the shot.
Fixed an issue where using a puzzle item may be unresponsive if there is other interactables nearby.

We're pleased to announce v1.7 of Outbreak: Epidemic has been released. This patch includes improvements to the camera system - namely allowing you to set camera distance and height! You can change these directly in the Options menu or change them ingame via the new key bindings (check the Controls menu)!

This patch also includes some fixes to the Tom model to adjust how he holds both the Handgun and SMG to make aiming more natural. It also includes some item text fixes to clearly denote melee weapons only usable by Renault.

Thanks again for playing! Remember - if you're enjoying the game and feel it deserves it, please consider filing a positive review. If you hit any issues, please reach out to me before filing a negative review as I may be able to help fix it! :)
Reach out anytime in the forums or on our official Discord! See the forums for the link to the Discord.
Thanks and have fun! :)
We're happy to announce v1.6 of Outbreak: Epidemic has been released! This patch greatly focuses on improving the single-player experience.

When playing in Single-Player Mode, you will now have a much larger inventory by default to offset your lack of teammates. Characters like the Renegade will still get their inventory buffs, but now this makes most of the other characters viable!

In addition, on Easy and Normal difficulty, you will now find more supplies on both Realism Mode and Arcade Mode, and encounter fewer powerful enemies when you're assaulted by mobs. This primarily took the form of reducing the number of Reptiles thrown at you at once in set piece moments.

Thank you everyone for your feedback! We've had an awesome week of growth for the game! Remember - if you're enjoying the game, be sure to leave a positive review and share your thoughts. If you hit issues, bugs, or have feedback, reach out to me anytime before filing a negative review - I might be able to help fix it quick!
Also, we pushed a quick patch v1.61 that allows you to disable the Weather in the Options menu. This may help with lower-end computers trying to run the game. Enjoy!
Note 2 - We just released v1.62 which fixed the issue where changing your player side (left or right) in the main menu didn't work correctly.
We're happy to announce the v1.5 patch for Outbreak: Epidemic is released! This release contains a major new feature - realism mode - based on the huge amount of feedback we've received.
Please post feedback on Realism Mode here!

Realism Mode - This brand new way of playing Outbreak: Epidemic notches up the realism by significantly boosting headshot damage - meaning many standard enemies could be killed in a single well placed headshot. But as a trade-off, you now have much less resources to work with. You need to make every bullet count if you want to survive. Advanced monsters can still take a beating, but your only way to defeat them is by going for the head! NOTE: Like the old way Epidemic played? It's still available - just switch back to Arcade Mode in your game lobby!
Fixed an issue where quick weapon switching could happen while menus are up.
The blood effects when you take damage are now toned way down and will not obscure much of the screen.
Weapons now zoom in when aiming.
A rare issue where flashlights would become very dim is fixed.

We're happy to announce Outbreak: Epidemic v1.4 has been released. This patch includes new functionality that has been highly requested - the ability to always face the camera and to switch the side your player appears on. Keep submitting feedback!

Remember, if you're enjoying the game and feel it deserves it, please consider filing a positive review and sharing your thoughts. If you hit any issues, please reach out prior to a negative review to see if we can address your issue!

Players can now change their view to always have the character face the camera direction. You can set this setting in the Options menu or change it during gameplay anytime via the new key binding. NOTE: If you played Outbreak: Epidemic before, you will need to either reset controls to default or manually bind to use this functionality in realtime.

Players can now set their player position on either the left or right side of the screen. You can set this in the Options menu or change it during gameplay anytime via the new key binding. NOTE: If you played Outbreak: Epidemic before, you will need to either reset controls to default or manually bind to use this functionality in realtime.
The music toggle in the Options menu now clearly displays whether the music is enabled or disabled on the button text.
You can now bind the B button on your gamepad in the Controls menu.
Weather effects now follow properly in spectator view and correctly shut off when your spectated target is indoors.
We're pleased to announce Outbreak: Epidemic v1.2 has been released with some highly requested features!

Players can now equip/switch weapons realtime without using their inventory in the Handgun, Shotgun/SMG, Power & Melee categories via new bindings. NOTE: You need to either reset the game controls to default OR bind these functions if you've played Outbreak: Epidemic before. Inventory cooldown times still apply on weapon switching.

Players can now sprint using the new Run binding. Players have a limited amount of stamina that allows them to sprint which automatically recharges when they are not sprinting. NOTE: You need to either reset the game controls to default OR bind the Run function directly to use it.
Player movement speeds have been adjusted. When aiming or crouching, players move at reduced speed. Players cannot sprint while aiming or crouching.

The default key bindings for Keyboard & Gamepad have been changed due to the new functionality above. It is highly recommended you reset your controls to default in the Controls menu if you've played Outbreak: Epidemic before.
All weapons are now available for trial on the Tutorial scenario.
Hi All,
Thank you for all the feedback everyone has been sharing over the past day since release. It's been great to see so many folks playing and enjoying Epidemic.

I have taken some time to go through as many of the reviews as I could and gather up some quick fixes to help improve the game experience (like mouse sensitivity, volume settings, glare intensity and more!). Other areas I'll be working on next include weapon switching, and a few other hotly requested features.
In the meantime, enjoy the fixes in v1.1 which is now available.
Game version bumped to v1.1. You must update to play with other players running this version.

Minor buff to player movement speed. NOTE: This will continue to be evaluated, including potential run functionality, in future patches. The goal is to find the middle ground where movement feels swift but players do not have too great speed versus their enemies.
Mouse sensitivity added to the Controls menu.
Game Volume can now be more discretely set from 0-10. NOTE: You will need to reset your volume to your desired level on next game load if you've played Outbreak: Epidemic before.
Enemies can no longer be incapacitated prior to death. The first time an enemy is knocked down, it is truly dead and will not reanimate.
Player damage buffed on Easy (+35% total) and Normal Difficulty (+20% total).
Lowered the intensity of general environment lighting in many locations.
Lowered the intensity of the player's flashlight.
Lumberjack life leech changed to 20% per level.
An additional Aid Spray added earlier in the Outbreak scenario.
